maria: Heads-up — during atlas-13k int4v2 bring-up I hit a reproducible coherence drop around token ~9k with dynamic tiling. Responses become short and off-topic.

jon: Minimal repro? KV dumps?

maria: Small repro:
```python
from rwclient import Client
c = Client(model='atlas-13k-int4v2')
ctx = 'SYS:\n' + 'A'*8800 + '\n'
for i in range(100):
  ctx += f'user{i}: q?\n'
print(c.generate(ctx, max_tokens=400, kv_inspect=True).text)
```
KV dump attached to CI run.

ravi: I inspected the dump. There's a hole: indices 22656..24603 missing, everything before/after present. Gap == 1948? looks like a tiling stride (we use 2k-ish).

jon: Any compaction/gc log entries at the same timestamp?

ravi: Logs: 
[2026-03-10T08:11:02Z] compactor: select_stride=2048
[2026-03-10T08:11:02Z] kv: apply_compaction removed=2048
No explicit eviction RPC. Also RoPE phase mismatch across the hole.

maria: Reverting recent compaction heuristic (PR #6890) on my local branch removed the gap and the model stayed coherent past 12k.

jon: Likely a bookkeeping off-by-one in compaction when tail tiles are partially filled. Plan: add assert ensuring kv_index_map monotonicity post-compact, emit diagnostic dump with tile_offsets + pos_scale on failure. Add unit test simulating partial tiles.

ravi: I'll run fuzz with timing jitter overnight against dynamic-tiling + int4v2. If assert trips, capture raw pages to s3://redwood-ci/bugs/3311223344/

ops-bot: ci job 8122 queued (gpu-2).

maria: Thanks. Tagging high-impact for bring-up. Will prepare a canary if patch is small.
